# Team attack runs: quick start

The short, exact version of `engineering/P3_TEAM_ATTACK_RUNBOOK.md` (read that for the
reasons). Commands were checked against the CLI and the lab on 2026-10-28.
**Attack traffic is generated by the team, with their own tools, from ATK01, against
WAF01 only.** The project contains no attack generator and never will.

## 0. Simulated tests vs real attack evaluation (do not mix them)

| | Synthetic regression cases (P6) | Team attack runs (this document) |
|---|---|---|
| What | Feature-level counts (e.g. "+12 failed logins") added to recorded benign windows in memory | Real packets from real tools through FW01 → WAF01 → APP01 |
| Traffic sent | **None** | Yes |
| Labelled | `SYNTHETIC` | ATTACK source with `attack_type` from the run journal |
| Answers | "Did a model change make the detectors less sensitive?" (regression) | "Does the system detect, contain and respond to real attacks?" |
| Can support a detection claim | **No** (the evaluator refuses synthetic data) | Yes, with run-level CIs |

## 1. Where each command runs

| Where | What | Shell |
|---|---|---|
| **Host** (repo `~/uot/ai-adaptive-firewall`) | scenario journal, kill switch, watchdog, manifest | `uv run afw scenario ...` |
| **CTRL01** | dataset capture, validation, evaluation | `afwc ...` (alias below) |
| **ATK01** (10.77.10.10) | the attack tool, **installed by the team** (nothing but curl is installed today) | `ssh -F ~/.config/afw/ssh_config atk01` |
| **USR01** | benign background users | `ssh -F ~/.config/afw/ssh_config usr01` |

On CTRL01 (`ssh -F ~/.config/afw/ssh_config ctrl01`):

```bash
alias afwc='sudo -u afwctl env -C /var/lib/afw AFW_CONFIG=/etc/afw/lab.yaml AFW_DATA_DIR=/var/lib/afw AFW_API_TOKENS_FILE=/etc/afw/secrets/api_tokens.yaml /opt/afw/venv/bin/afw'
```

## 2. Addresses and targets (fixed)

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Attacker | **10.77.10.10** (ATK01; the only attacker in the registry) |
| Target | **https://10.77.30.10/** (WAF01:443). Ports 22, 80 and 3306 only for `net-portscan` (blocked by FW01, IDS-visible) |
| Never target | 10.77.50.0/24 (management), 10.77.60.0/24 (database), anything else |
| Benign background | **10.77.20.200–.249**, two new addresses per run, never reused. Taken: .10–.197 |

Scenarios (`uv run afw scenario list`):

| Scenario | Family | Max | Runs needed |
|---|---|---|---|
| `web-bruteforce-login` | credential_bruteforce | 900 s | 3 test + 1 validation |
| `web-sqli-probe` | sql_injection | 900 s | 3 test + 1 validation |
| `web-content-discovery` | content_discovery | 900 s | 3 test + 1 validation |
| `net-portscan` | port_scan | 600 s | 3 test + 1 validation |
| `low-and-slow-bruteforce` | credential_bruteforce_slow | 3600 s | 3, **holdout: last, evaluated once** |

Runs of one family must be separate sessions, hours apart.

## 3. Before every run

```bash
# host
uv run afw lab status                    # 8 VMs started
uv run afw lab verify                    # every check passed (41/41)
curl -s --cacert ~/.config/afw/pki/lab-ca.pem https://10.77.50.10:8080/api/health \
  | python3 -c 'import json,sys; h=json.load(sys.stdin); print(h["status"], h["mode"], "degraded" if h["telemetry_degraded"] else "telemetry ok")'
# expect: ok monitor telemetry ok   (detection runs are in MONITOR mode)
uv run afw scenario watchdog &           # keep running during the run (stops ATK01 past max duration)
```

## 4. One run (example: `web-sqli-probe`, background .200/.201)

```bash
# 1. host, t = -5 min: benign background (the P6 v2 generator is already on USR01;
#    after a USR01 reboot first: scp -F ~/.config/afw/ssh_config traffic/benign_personas.py usr01:/tmp/benign_personas_v2.py)
ssh -F ~/.config/afw/ssh_config usr01 'for ip in 10.77.20.200 10.77.20.201; do
  sudo ip addr add $ip/24 dev ens3 2>/dev/null
  AFW_MODE=personas AFW_PERSONA_SET=v2 AFW_SOURCES=$ip AFW_DURATION=1800 AFW_SEED=${ip##*.} \
    setsid nohup python3 /tmp/benign_personas_v2.py >/tmp/bg_$ip.log 2>&1 </dev/null &
done'

# 2. host, t = 0: open the run BEFORE starting the tool
uv run afw scenario begin web-sqli-probe <your-name> --notes "sqlmap 1.8 --level 1; bg .200,.201"
#    -> prints RUN_ID

# 3. ATK01: start your tool against https://10.77.30.10/ only
# 4. host, at each phase change:  uv run afw scenario mark <RUN_ID> "phase 2: ..."
# 5. ATK01: stop the tool FIRST, then host:
uv run afw scenario end <RUN_ID>
#    emergency (wrong target, runaway tool): uv run afw scenario abort <RUN_ID> "<reason>"  (powers ATK01 off)

# 6. host, after the benign tail (t = end + 5 min): write the manifest and copy it to CTRL01
uv run afw scenario manifest <RUN_ID> /tmp/<RUN_ID>.json --benign 10.77.20.200,10.77.20.201
scp -F ~/.config/afw/ssh_config /tmp/<RUN_ID>.json ctrl01:/tmp/

# 7. CTRL01: capture and validate
afwc dataset capture atk-sqli-20261101-1 --manifest /tmp/<RUN_ID>.json --purpose test
afwc dataset validate atk-sqli-20261101-1       # exit 1 = any FAIL -> do not use it
```

Labels come from the journal, never from memory: ATK01 is `attack` with the scenario's
`attack_type` inside the begin–end window; the two background addresses are `benign`.
`--purpose`: `test` for the 3 series runs, `validation` for the 1 run per family that
feeds the promotion gate, `holdout` for low-and-slow.

## 5. What to check after each run

| Check | Expected |
|---|---|
| `dataset validate` | no FAIL. Copy every WARN line into the run log |
| `labelled_sources_observed` WARN for ATK01 | normal for `net-portscan` (FW01 drops it before the app); say so |
| Dashboard, or `GET /api/sources/10.77.10.10` and `GET /api/assessments` (token) | the attacker appears with its evidence categories; in monitor mode, proposals only |
| Pure brute force (ADR-039) | **prediction**: strict rate limit with `insufficient_corroboration_for_block`, not a block. Record what actually happens |
| Background users | should not be restricted; any restriction is a false positive and is reported |

Record per run: RUN_ID, dataset id, tool and version, options, start/end, operator, and
any problems. **Every begun run is reported, including aborted ones.**

## 6. After a family's runs (the agent can do this from here)

```bash
afwc experiment evaluate --datasets <ids> --streaming --warmup p6-final,p6-final-shift --out /tmp/eval-<family>.json
```

This gives static, frozen-ML, streaming-ML and hybrid arms with recall, precision, FPR,
containment, latency, CIs over runs. Then one run per family in **enforce** mode (admin
switches the mode, back to monitor afterwards) shows real containment; it is reported
separately.

## 7. Never

* Attack from anywhere but ATK01, or target anything but the registry targets.
* Use replayed or synthetic attack files as evidence.
* Change thresholds, models or profiles between runs of a series.
* Re-run until the numbers look better.
